Hydrocarbon, or Ethanol machines for cannabis oil extraction.

## EQUIPMENT AND PRODUCTS

PURE5™ is the most innovative botanical extraction equipment company focusing on cannabis and hemp.
Our superior technology gently extracts botanicals, delivers full natural potency, and has set a new
higher level of standards in the cannabis industry.

### HTE Extraction Systems

[ View all ][85]

### **R134a Aerosol Extraction Systems**

High Terpene Extraction (HTE) is perfect for extracting the fine oil fraction from every botanical.
The extraction process is gentle to the oil and the plant material, using low pressure, room
temperature, and delivers naturally potent terpene rich full-spectrum oil. It collects the complete
terpene and cannabinoid profile without degradation of components.

Our R134a [solventless cannabis extraction equipments][86] are:
* 20 Liter MAX CBD/THC extraction machine: ideal for small-scale extraction operations
* 50 Liter CBD/THC extraction machines: ideal for small to mid-scale extraction operations
* 100 Liter CBD/THC extraction machines: ideal for mid-scale scale extraction operations
* 200 Liter systems: Ideal for medium to large commercial operations
* 500 Liter systems: For large-capacity commercial production
* 1000 Liter systems: Ideal for very-large-scale production

### 1500L Ethanol Extraction System

[ View all ][87]

### **Ethanol CBD/**THC Extraction Equipment** (EtOH) – 20-1000L Ethanol Extraction System**

Ethanol is a universal solvent with power in resin and alkaloid extraction. We pair the R134a
aerosol and EtOH extraction to extract any plant material. Our [ethanol cannabis extraction
system][88] utilize a chemical process that feeds the material continuously via a conveyor into the
extraction vessel and delivers a consistent output of purified oil.
* 20-1000 liter EtOH extraction equipment: Get a better quality final product by eliminating
undesired compounds and preserve all terpenes and cannabinoids.
* Easy evaporation results in clean and pure extract without traces of solvent
* Easy-to-use Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and touchscreen interface
* Fully automatic with all safety features. Users can program pressure, temperature, and time.

### Post Processing & Test Lab Equipment Systems

[ View all ][89]

### **Lab Equipment – Post Processing & Test Lab Equipment Systems**

PURE5™ provides own-build, high-quality [cannabis lab testing equipment][90], including stainless
steel molecular systems for the distillation process, various sizes of vacuum industrial ovens, THC
remediation equipment, stainless steel isomerization, and crystallization reactors, and gas
chromatography equipment.
* **50L Crystallization Reactor**: Produce high-quality cannabis isolate from various plant sources
with minimal impurities and no residual solvents or other unwanted compounds.
* **Gas Chromatography**: Quick and low-cost analyses of potency, residual solvents and terpenes and
the quantification of their concentrations according to molecular weight and boiling point.
* **50L – 500L Vacuum** Oven: Dry, Decas and Decarboxylate cannabis extracts and activate the
cannabinoids in the extract at low temperatures and pressures, allowing for a more efficient
extraction process.
* **20L-200L HTE**: More efficient extraction. The lower temperatures also reduce the risk of
burning off valuable compounds while allowing for more precise control over the extraction
temperature and times for optimal cannabinoid potency.

### THC Remediation Equipment

[ View all ][91]

### **THC Remediation Systems and Equipment**

Our patented [THC Remediation equipment][92] is a first and only of its kind in the hemp industry.
It uses a dynamic combination of gas, low heat, and low pressure to isomerize THC into other
cannabinoids such as CBD, CBC, CBN, etc.
* Fully organic remediation process uses no solvents.
* Easy-to-use, fully automated system
* DEA compliant
* 5 liter – 150 liter/day processing capacity range for small to large-scale commercial production

## Cannabis Distillation Equipment

PURE5™ [cannabis distillation equipment][93] is designed for high-quality, large-batch cannabis
extraction. They use a highly efficient and reliable wiped-film distillation process to separate and
purify compounds in cannabis oils. The system features a two-stage thin film process, whereby the
rotation of a heated rotor element creates a thin film on the inside wall of the distillation
vessel. This process is highly efficient and can achieve very high-quality separations of compounds
in cannabis oils.

### The 6" SS Wipe Film Distillation System

[ Tech Information ][94]

### The 6″ SS Wipe Film Distillation system

Made of 304 or 316 stainless steel and can process faster compared to its glass counterpart. This is
because stainless steel has a higher heat transfer rate, resulting in more than double the
processing capacity of conventional glass wipe film distillation systems.

The SS system also features a ball valve discharge system that automates the flow rate and also
provides increased safety during the distillation process.

### The 6" GL Wipe Film Distillation system

[ More about the 6"GL ][95]

### The 6″ GL Wipe Film Distillation system

Made of food-grade glass can process up to 7 liters/hour and features a fully automated terpene and
solvent recovery collection systems, allowing for easy collection and storage of the distillate. It
also includes a unique filtration system that removes unwanted solids to ensure the highest quality
product.

#### Main features of the PURE5™ Wipe Film Distillation Systems
* Fast and efficient distillation
* High quality and purity of the final product
* Precise temperature control
* Ease of operation with automated systems
* Safe and efficient solvent recovery
* Cost-effective solution with low maintenance requirements.

## Farming Equipment

### Hemp Harvester

[ Harvester Tech Data ][96]

### Hemp Harvester

Our robust hemp harvester is a specialized agricultural machine for harvesting and collecting hemp
plants. It combines cutting, gathering, and baling hemp plants into one process. The harvester has
adjustable settings for the length and thickness of plant stems, allowing for various harvesting
styles.

### The 10T Conveyor Dryer System

[ Dryer Tech Info ][97]

### 10T Conveyor Dryer System

The dryer is composed of a heated chamber that circulates and dries the plants with warm to hot dry
air, similar to a convection oven. A 22KW heat exchange furnace generates the necessary heat from
25C to 60C to dry the plants, while a control cabinet controls temperature, airflow, power, and
other variables to ensure optimal drying conditions.

### Stick and Seed Separation

[ More about the Separator ][98]

### Stick and Seed Separation

Our Stick and Seed Separation system separates hemp sticks from flower and seeds for further
processing. Then further separates the seeds from flower in 4 fractions.
* The food-grade stainless steel feeding conveyor moves the hemp material from the drying process to
the sifter.
* The sifter uses a vibratory motion to separate the hemp sticks from the seeds that are light
enough to roll down the mesh.
* They then pass through a blower cyclone system to further separate the large particles from the
smaller ones.
* The control cabinet allows users to ensure optimal power, speed, and temperature as the sticks are
sorted and separated.

The end result is a clean, dry batch of seeds ready for further processing or sale.

## Our product categories

We craft products for today, tomorrow, and beyond with unparalleled knowledge of how to make what
patients need
[7][7]

### Oral Solutions

Oral solutions are carefully crafted to deliver consistent and accurate dosages, ensuring reliable
effects for patients. Oral solutions provide a user-friendly alternative for patients looking to
integrate cannabis into their treatment regimen with precision and ease. SOMAÍ’s oral solutions
portfolio, based on three full spectrum cannabis extracts’ types, combines a large range of THC/CBD
ratios to cover a wide variety of medical conditions.
[Untitled 1920 x 950 px 1][Untitled 1920 x 950 px 1]

### Proprietary formulations

Proprietary formulations represent unique and specialized blends to address specific therapeutic
needs. These formulations involve a proprietary combination of cannabinoids, terpenes, and other
compounds, tailored to provide enhanced efficacy and targeted relief for specific medical
conditions. SOMAÍ’s proprietary 10:10 series is a combination of different excipients, terpenes and
nano emulsions designed for various conditions.
[SOMAI IG Size 1920 x 950 px 6][SOMAI IG Size 1920 x 950 px 6]

### Inhalation Oils

Designed for vaporization, these formulations allow controlled cannabinoid inhalation without
traditional smoking’s combustion. The fast onset of effects makes vape oils a preferred choice for
those seeking rapid relief. Vape oils provide patients with a modern and efficient way to
incorporate cannabis into their treatment plans. Our premium vape oil available in multiple distinct
terpene formulas, is an alternative to vaporizing dried flower.
[4][4]

### Oral sprays

The spray delivery format provides convenient administration with precise dosage with a peppermint
taste profile in a balanced THC/CBD ratio. The fast onset of effects makes them suitable for
patients seeking quick relief. Additionally, oral sprays’ compact and portable nature enhances their
accessibility, allowing patients to manage their symptoms conveniently throughout the day.
[5][5]

### Soft Gel capsules

The soft gel capsule delivery format allows comfortable administration and precise dosage for the
convenience of patients. Soft gel capsules are easy to swallow, making them a convenient option for
patients who prefer oral administration. The standardized dosing and ease of integration into daily
routines make soft gel capsules a practical and patient-friendly option for those seeking the
benefits of cannabinoids in a pharmaceutical-grade form.
[6][6]

### Dried Cannabis Flower

Dried medical cannabis flower is a natural and unprocessed form of therapeutic cannabis, containing
a diverse array of cannabinoids. It offers a versatile way to manage symptoms and provides
customized and fast relief, particularly beneficial in medical conditions requiring a rapid onset.
SOMAÍ procures high-quality GMP flowers utilizing selected cultivars grown both indoors and
greenhouse.
[Newsletter (32)][Newsletter (32)]

### Oral Gums

Oral Gums are innovative pharmaceutical formulations designed to cater to the unique therapeutic
requirements of patients with specific needs. Combining ease of use with a pleasant experience,
these gums ensure a practical and effective delivery of cannabinoids, making them an excellent
option for personalized care.

### Our Mission

At Waterside Pharmaceuticals, every decision is guided by a deep sense of care, responsibility and
driven by our commitment to deliver safe, efficacious and cost-effective medicine that transforms
the lives of millions. We believe true quality in medicinal cannabis comes from combining human
dedication with cutting-edge technology, so you can trust that each batch is consistently pure and
effective.

Our UK-based, fully controlled indoor facility empowers us to oversee every detail, from bespoke LED
lighting and climate control to pest-free growing and rainwater harvesting. This hands-on approach
ensures each plant receives the attention it deserves.

Sustainability isn’t an afterthought; it’s at the heart of how we operate. We run on green-tariff
energy today and are developing off-grid capabilities for tomorrow. Closed-loop irrigation and
zero-waste protocols mean minimal environmental impact, so patients and the planet both benefit.

Operating under GACP and GDP standards (and aspiring to GMP) our processes are designed to ensure
batch-to-batch consistency and full traceability. Rigorous in-house checks and Certificate of
Analysis releases help ensure every vial meets the highest quality expectations.

Together, these principles form the foundation of our promise: to provide premium, locally produced
medicinal cannabis that puts patient welfare and environmental stewardship first.

#### What Sets Waterside Apart

At Waterside, we approach cannabis cultivation with the precision and care expected in
pharmaceutical manufacturing. Our fully indoor, vertically integrated facility in Aberdeenshire
operates using Total Controlled Environment Agriculture (TCEA), allowing us to optimise light,
climate, and nutrients for consistent plant development.

Every phase of our process is governed by a robust Quality Management System. While we are not yet
GMP-certified, we operate to GACP and GDP standards and apply the foundations GMP principles
throughout delivering batch-to-batch uniformity and full traceability from clone to certificate of
analysis.

Rooted in our local community and driven by sustainable practices - including rainwater harvesting,
renewable energy, and a closed-loop nutrient recycling -Waterside aims to be part of a resilient UK

Austranna in South East Queensland: Harnessing Innovation

Pictured: Austranna facility, Scenic Rim QLD

Austranna’s facility in South East Queensland is a pioneering example of advanced medicinal cannabis cultivation. This strategic location offers unique benefits that align perfectly with our innovative approach to growing medicinal cannabis.

Solar-Powered Sustainability in a Subtropical Climate

The facility is classed as a Hybrid-Indoor Glasshouse, and leverages South East Queensland’s abundant sunshine, harnessing solar energy to power a significant portion of our operations. This use of renewable energy is in sync with the region's long sunshine hours, reducing our reliance on non-renewable power sources and significantly lowering our carbon footprint. The subtropical climate of the area provides an ideal external environment, enhancing the efficiency of our solar-powered system.

Advanced Control in a Natural Setting

The facility design allows us to create a meticulously controlled cultivation environment, essential for producing high-quality medicinal cannabis. While enjoying the natural light and warmth from Queensland’s climate, our facility can regulate internal conditions to ensure optimal plant growth. This combination of natural and controlled factors results in a more sustainable cultivation process, minimising the need for artificial inputs while maximising plant health and product quality.

Strategic Location for Market Accessibility and Talent Pool

Positioned near Brisbane and other large urban centres, our facility enjoys easy access to key markets and a skilled workforce. This proximity enables efficient distribution of our products and allows us to tap into a pool of talented professionals, essential for running a high-tech cultivation operation like ours.

Cultivating Innovation and Community Ties

In line with Queensland’s supportive stance on the medicinal cannabis industry, our location fosters opportunities for innovation and collaboration. We engage in partnerships with research institutions and industry experts, driving advancements in cannabis cultivation and processing. Furthermore, our presence in South East Queensland goes beyond business operations; it’s about embedding ourselves in the community, supporting local economies, and practising environmental stewardship.

Environmental and Social Responsibility

Our facility’s design and location reflect Austranna’s commitment to environmental and social responsibility. By utilising solar energy in our Hybrid-Indoor Glasshouse, we set a standard for sustainable practices in the industry. Our approach in South East Queensland is a testament to our dedication to being a responsible and innovative leader in the global medicinal cannabis market.

Our Commitment to Sustainabilility through Medicinal Cannabis Cultivation

Pictured: Austranna Facility

Austranna's Commitment to Sustainability in Medicinal Cannabis Cultivation

In an industry that is rapidly evolving, Austranna stands at the forefront of sustainable practices in medicinal cannabis cultivation. Our hybrid-indoor glasshouse facility in Queensland, embodies our commitment to environmental stewardship while meeting the growing demand for medicinal cannabis.

Energy Efficiency in Cultivation

One of the significant environmental impacts of cannabis cultivation is its energy usage, especially when cultivation occurs indoors. Recognising this, Austranna has taken proactive steps to mitigate energy consumption. Our hybrid-indoor glasshouse integrates advanced technology to harness solar power, significantly reducing our reliance on traditional energy sources. This approach aligns with industry trends, where there’s a growing interest in transitioning from fully enclosed indoor environments to more energy-efficient greenhouse setups.

Water Conservation and Efficient Use

Water usage is another critical aspect of sustainability in cannabis cultivation. It's known that both indoor and outdoor cannabis growing can be water-intensive. At Austranna, we have implemented state-of-the-art irrigation systems, such as drip irrigation, to optimise water usage. These systems, equipped with sensors, allow for precise control of water application, ensuring that plants receive the exact amount needed for optimal growth, thus preventing water wastage.

Reducing Environmental Footprint

The cannabis industry, as it grows, faces challenges related to its environmental footprint, which includes energy consumption, water use, and waste generation. At Austranna, we continuously explore ways to minimise our environmental impact. From using energy-efficient equipment and renewable energy sources to adopting sustainable waste management practices, every aspect of our operation is designed to reduce our carbon footprint.

Sustainable Practices: The Way Forward

Acknowledging that data on energy and water use, air emissions, and waste from the cannabis industry are limited, Austranna is committed to filling these data gaps. Our approach is not just about compliance but about setting a higher standard in the industry. Moving cannabis cultivation outdoors to decrease energy use may not always be feasible due to environmental constraints, such as drought conditions. OUR STORY

**Austranna is a family-owned business that began in 2018 with the acquisition of land in
Queensland, Australia. Our farm is home to a large, protected cropping, ornamental tree nursery, a
state-of-the-art tissue culture laboratory, a five-hectare Venlo-style hybrid glasshouse and an
8,500m2 GMP manufacturing facility.**

Austranna has developed as a practical response to the evolving needs of our family. We initially
invested in a commercial farm to grow vegetables and herbs, but with the onset of COVID-19 we
adapted by diversifying into ornamental crops.

The acquisition of a neighbouring camel farm has enabled us to expand our operational capacity, and
it lay the groundwork for Austranna as it stands today. With added lands, we secured water rights
and room for an extensive solar farm, essential steps towards self-sufficiency and environmental
stewardship.

Today, Austranna’s operations extend far beyond traditional agriculture. We’re using our land for
renewable energy projects and planning for future expansions that align with our core values of
sustainability and innovation. This journey from a vegetable and herb farm to a multifaceted
agricultural enterprise reflects our approach to business: adapt, innovate and always plan for the
future.

Austranna in South East Queensland: Harnessing Innovation

Pictured: Austranna facility, Scenic Rim QLD

Austranna’s facility in South East Queensland is a pioneering example of advanced medicinal cannabis cultivation. This strategic location offers unique benefits that align perfectly with our innovative approach to growing medicinal cannabis.

Solar-Powered Sustainability in a Subtropical Climate

The facility is classed as a Hybrid-Indoor Glasshouse, and leverages South East Queensland’s abundant sunshine, harnessing solar energy to power a significant portion of our operations. This use of renewable energy is in sync with the region's long sunshine hours, reducing our reliance on non-renewable power sources and significantly lowering our carbon footprint. The subtropical climate of the area provides an ideal external environment, enhancing the efficiency of our solar-powered system.

Advanced Control in a Natural Setting

The facility design allows us to create a meticulously controlled cultivation environment, essential for producing high-quality medicinal cannabis. While enjoying the natural light and warmth from Queensland’s climate, our facility can regulate internal conditions to ensure optimal plant growth. This combination of natural and controlled factors results in a more sustainable cultivation process, minimising the need for artificial inputs while maximising plant health and product quality.

Strategic Location for Market Accessibility and Talent Pool

Positioned near Brisbane and other large urban centres, our facility enjoys easy access to key markets and a skilled workforce. This proximity enables efficient distribution of our products and allows us to tap into a pool of talented professionals, essential for running a high-tech cultivation operation like ours.

Cultivating Innovation and Community Ties

In line with Queensland’s supportive stance on the medicinal cannabis industry, our location fosters opportunities for innovation and collaboration. We engage in partnerships with research institutions and industry experts, driving advancements in cannabis cultivation and processing. Furthermore, our presence in South East Queensland goes beyond business operations; it’s about embedding ourselves in the community, supporting local economies, and practising environmental stewardship.

Environmental and Social Responsibility

Our facility’s design and location reflect Austranna’s commitment to environmental and social responsibility. By utilising solar energy in our Hybrid-Indoor Glasshouse, we set a standard for sustainable practices in the industry. Our approach in South East Queensland is a testament to our dedication to being a responsible and innovative leader in the global medicinal cannabis market.

Our Commitment to Sustainabilility through Medicinal Cannabis Cultivation

Pictured: Austranna Facility

Austranna's Commitment to Sustainability in Medicinal Cannabis Cultivation

In an industry that is rapidly evolving, Austranna stands at the forefront of sustainable practices in medicinal cannabis cultivation. Our hybrid-indoor glasshouse facility in Queensland, embodies our commitment to environmental stewardship while meeting the growing demand for medicinal cannabis.

Energy Efficiency in Cultivation

One of the significant environmental impacts of cannabis cultivation is its energy usage, especially when cultivation occurs indoors. Recognising this, Austranna has taken proactive steps to mitigate energy consumption. Our hybrid-indoor glasshouse integrates advanced technology to harness solar power, significantly reducing our reliance on traditional energy sources. This approach aligns with industry trends, where there’s a growing interest in transitioning from fully enclosed indoor environments to more energy-efficient greenhouse setups.

Water Conservation and Efficient Use

Water usage is another critical aspect of sustainability in cannabis cultivation. It's known that both indoor and outdoor cannabis growing can be water-intensive. At Austranna, we have implemented state-of-the-art irrigation systems, such as drip irrigation, to optimise water usage. These systems, equipped with sensors, allow for precise control of water application, ensuring that plants receive the exact amount needed for optimal growth, thus preventing water wastage.

Reducing Environmental Footprint

The cannabis industry, as it grows, faces challenges related to its environmental footprint, which includes energy consumption, water use, and waste generation. At Austranna, we continuously explore ways to minimise our environmental impact. From using energy-efficient equipment and renewable energy sources to adopting sustainable waste management practices, every aspect of our operation is designed to reduce our carbon footprint.

Sustainable Practices: The Way Forward

Acknowledging that data on energy and water use, air emissions, and waste from the cannabis industry are limited, Austranna is committed to filling these data gaps. Our approach is not just about compliance but about setting a higher standard in the industry. Moving cannabis cultivation outdoors to decrease energy use may not always be feasible due to environmental constraints, such as drought conditions. Therefore, our hybrid-indoor glasshouse facility, with its controlled environment and sustainability-focused practices, represents a significant step towards a greener future in medicinal cannabis cultivation.

At Austranna, we believe that sustainability is not just a practice but a responsibility. Our efforts in creating an eco-friendly cultivation environment demonstrate our commitment to preserving the planet while providing high-quality medicinal cannabis products. As the industry continues to grow, we are dedicated to leading by example, showing that it is possible to balance business objectives with environmental consciousness.

Australia's Medicinal Cannabis Framework: A Comprehensive Approach to Regulation and Safety

The Foundation of Medicinal Cannabis Regulation in Australia

Australia’s medicinal cannabis regulatory framework is a prime example of the country's dedication to public health and safety, balanced with ensuring access to essential medication for those in need. This system is the result of meticulous coordination between state and Commonwealth legislatures, adhering to both national policies and international conventions like the United Nations' Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs 1961.

Narcotic Drugs Act 1967: The Cornerstone of Medicinal Cannabis Control

Central to Australia's regulatory landscape is the Commonwealth Narcotic Drugs Act 1967, which sets the legal parameters for the cultivation of cannabis for medicinal purposes within the nation. This Act explicitly prohibits personal cultivation for medicinal purposes and recreational cannabis cultivation and importation, underscoring the government's commitment to regulating cannabis within strict legal bounds.

2016 Amendments: Paving the Way for Medicinal Cannabis Access

A pivotal development in Australia’s medicinal cannabis policy was the implementation of the medicinal cannabis scheme in 2016 through the Narcotic Drugs Amendment Act 2016. This groundbreaking amendment facilitated the legal cultivation, production, and research of medicinal cannabis, marking a significant shift in policy and providing a regulated pathway for patient access to medicinal cannabis.

Therapeutic Goods Act 1989: Ensuring Quality and Safety

Supporting this framework are crucial amendments to the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989. These modifications are vital in managing regulatory approvals and access to unapproved medicinal cannabis products, ensuring they meet stringent standards of quality and safety before being supplied in Australia.

Classification and Control: Safeguarding Public Health

The legislative framework also includes classification under the Australian Poisons Standard, which dictates the categorisation of medicinal cannabis products based on their cannabinoid content. This classification system is a key component in the responsible management of medicinal cannabis distribution and use.

A Model of Effective Medicinal Cannabis Regulation

Australia's approach to medicinal cannabis regulation is a testament to its ability to adapt legislative frameworks to meet evolving societal needs while prioritising safety and control. The success of this framework lies in its versatility and careful regulation, showcasing Australia as a model of how to responsibly harness the therapeutic benefits of medicinal cannabis.

OUR STORY

**Austranna is a family-owned business that began in 2018 with the acquisition of land in
Queensland, Australia. Our farm is home to a large, protected cropping, ornamental tree nursery, a
state-of-the-art tissue culture laboratory, a five-hectare Venlo-style hybrid glasshouse and an
8,500m2 GMP manufacturing facility.**

Austranna has developed as a practical response to the evolving needs of our family. We initially
invested in a commercial farm to grow vegetables and herbs, but with the onset of COVID-19 we
adapted by diversifying into ornamental crops.

The acquisition of a neighbouring camel farm has enabled us to expand our operational capacity, and
it lay the groundwork for Austranna as it stands today. With added lands, we secured water rights
and room for an extensive solar farm, essential steps towards self-sufficiency and environmental
stewardship.

Today, Austranna’s operations extend far beyond traditional agriculture. We’re using our land for
renewable energy projects and planning for future expansions that align with our core values of
sustainability and innovation. This journey from a vegetable and herb farm to a multifaceted
agricultural enterprise reflects our approach to business: adapt, innovate and always plan for the
future.

# CANNABIS EXTRACTION SERVICES MINNESOTA

Professional, licensed cannabis and hemp extraction for cultivators across Minnesota. We maximize
the value of your harvest.

For licensed cannabis cultivators in Minnesota, the quality of your flower is only half the battle.
Transforming premium biomass into high-value extracts requires scientific expertise, specialized
equipment, and a deep understanding of the market. BSD Labs provides professional, reliable, and
fully compliant cannabis extraction services from our state-of-the-art facility in Waseca, MN.

## Our Extraction Methods

We offer a suite of extraction methods tailored to your specific product goals. Our process is not
one-size-fits-all — we match the method to your desired end-product to ensure optimal purity,
potency, and flavor profile.

Cryo-Ethanol

Chilled ethanol extraction for high-volume, full-spectrum oil production. Ideal for distillate,
edibles, and tinctures.

Best For: Distillate, Edibles, Tinctures
Hydrocarbon

Butane/propane extraction preserving the delicate terpene profiles of the cannabis plant. Produces
flavorful, aromatic concentrates.

Best For: Live Resin, Shatter, Wax, HTFSE
Solventless

Ice, water, and pressure only. The purest expression of the plant — no solvents, no compromise.

Best For: Live Rosin, Hash Rosin

## The BSD Labs Extraction Process

Every extraction run at BSD Labs follows a rigorous, documented process. We begin with a thorough
assessment of your biomass — moisture content, cannabinoid profile, and terpene composition — to
determine the optimal extraction parameters. Our chemists then execute the extraction with
precision, monitoring every variable to ensure maximum yield and purity.

Following extraction, the crude oil undergoes winterization, filtration, and decarboxylation before
proceeding to distillation or further refinement. The result is a clean, potent extract that meets
the highest standards of the Minnesota cannabis market.

## Quality Assurance & Compliance

BSD Labs operates in full compliance with all Minnesota Office of Cannabis Management (OCM)
regulations. Every batch of extract is tested by an independent, state-licensed laboratory for
potency, residual solvents, pesticides, heavy metals, and microbials. We provide a full Certificate
of Analysis (COA) with every order, giving you and your customers complete confidence in the
product.

# WHOLESALE CANNABIS DISTILLATE MINNESOTA

High-purity THC distillate available in bulk quantities for licensed Minnesota manufacturers,
brands, and retailers.

BSD Labs produces some of Minnesota's most consistent, high-purity cannabis distillate. Our
multi-pass distillation process refines crude cannabis oil into a clean, potent product testing
consistently above 90% THC. Available for wholesale purchase by licensed Minnesota cannabis
businesses.

## What is Cannabis Distillate?

Cannabis distillate is the most refined and purified form of cannabis oil. Through a process of
fractional distillation — using heat and vacuum pressure to separate compounds by their boiling
points — we isolate Delta-9-THC at its highest concentration. The result is a thick, translucent
amber oil with exceptional potency and versatility.

Because distillate has a neutral flavor profile, it is the preferred base oil for a wide range of
cannabis products, including vape cartridges, edibles, tinctures, capsules, and topicals. Its
consistent potency makes it the gold standard for manufacturers who need a reliable, predictable
ingredient.

## Our Distillation Process

Our distillation process begins with high-quality crude cannabis oil extracted from Minnesota-grown
biomass. The crude oil undergoes a rigorous winterization and filtration process to remove fats,
waxes, and lipids before entering our short-path distillation system.

We perform multiple distillation passes to achieve the highest possible purity. Each pass further
refines the oil, removing residual solvents, chlorophyll, and other unwanted compounds. The final
product is a clean, golden distillate that consistently tests above 90% total cannabinoids.

## Wholesale Pricing & Minimum Orders

We offer competitive wholesale pricing for licensed Minnesota cannabis businesses. Our pricing is
tiered based on volume, with significant discounts available for larger orders. Contact us directly
to discuss your specific needs and receive a custom quote. We work with businesses of all sizes,
from small craft brands to large-scale manufacturers.

05 — Cannabis Toll Processing · Minnesota

# CANNABIS TOLL PROCESSING MINNESOTA

Turn your biomass into high-value extract. BSD Labs provides efficient, compliant toll processing
for licensed Minnesota cultivators — you own the product, we do the work.

Cannabis toll processing is the most efficient way for licensed Minnesota cultivators to convert
their biomass into high-value extracts without the capital investment of building their own
extraction operation. BSD Labs provides a reliable, transparent, and fully OCM-compliant toll
processing service out of our Waseca, MN facility — you bring the biomass, we return premium extract
with full documentation.

## What is Cannabis Toll Processing?

Toll processing is a service arrangement where a licensed cultivator provides their own cannabis
biomass to a licensed processor — in this case, BSD Labs — who then extracts and refines the
material and returns the resulting concentrate to the cultivator. You retain ownership of your
material throughout the entire process and pay a processing fee based on the volume of biomass
processed.

This model is ideal for licensed Minnesota cultivators who want to maximize the value of their full
harvest — including trim, shake, and lower-grade flower — without investing hundreds of thousands of
dollars in extraction equipment, facility upgrades, and trained extraction staff.

## Why Minnesota Cultivators Choose Toll Processing

As Minnesota's adult-use cannabis market scales in 2026, cultivators face a critical decision:
invest in in-house extraction infrastructure, or partner with a licensed processor. For most
cultivators, toll processing is the smarter path — lower upfront cost, faster time to market, and
access to professional-grade equipment and expertise from day one.

BSD Labs operates out of Waseca, MN — centrally located in southern Minnesota — making us an
accessible processing partner for cultivators across the state. We work exclusively B2B with
licensed Minnesota businesses, and we run our facility with the same operational rigor we apply to
the brands we manufacture in-house — full chain of custody, documented SOPs, and a real
understanding of what brand operators need from a manufacturer.

## How Our Toll Processing Works

Submit Your Biomass

Deliver your licensed cannabis biomass to our Waseca, MN facility. We accept flower, trim, and shake
from licensed MN cultivators. Scheduling is flexible to accommodate your harvest timeline.

Intake & Assessment

Our team performs a full intake assessment including moisture content and cannabinoid profile
testing to determine optimal extraction parameters for your specific material.

Extraction & Refinement

We extract and refine your material using the method best suited to your biomass and desired
end-product — distillate, live resin, or rosin. Multi-pass distillation achieves 90%+ THC purity.

Quality Testing

The finished extract is tested by an independent lab for potency, residual solvents, pesticides, and
heavy metals. Every batch receives a full-panel Certificate of Analysis.

Return & Documentation

We return your extract along with a full Certificate of Analysis and complete batch documentation
for your OCM compliance records. Secure chain of custody is maintained throughout.

## Extraction Methods & Output Quality

BSD Labs uses cryo-ethanol and hydrocarbon extraction paired with multi-pass distillation to produce
distillate at 90%+ THC purity. The extraction method selected for your biomass is determined by your
material type and your desired end-product. We can produce:
* **THC Distillate** — 90%+ purity, ideal for vape cartridges, edibles, and tinctures
* **Live Resin** — full-spectrum extract preserving terpene profile, premium concentrate market
* **Crude Oil** — pre-refinement extract for cultivators who want further in-house processing

Every batch undergoes independent third-party lab testing for potency, residual solvents,
pesticides, and heavy metals before it leaves our facility.

## Pricing & Requirements

Our toll processing fees are competitive and fully transparent — no hidden charges, no surprise line
items. Pricing is based on the volume of biomass processed and the extraction method selected. To
use our toll processing service, you must hold a valid Minnesota cannabis cultivator or manufacturer
license issued by the Office of Cannabis Management (OCM).

Contact us directly for a custom quote based on your harvest volume, biomass type, and desired
output. We'll respond within one business day.

## Frequently Asked Questions — Cannabis Toll Processing Minnesota

What is cannabis toll processing?

Toll processing is a fee-for-service arrangement where you bring your licensed cannabis biomass to
BSD Labs, we extract and refine it into concentrate, and return the finished product to you. You
retain full ownership of your material throughout — you simply pay a processing fee based on volume.

Do I need a license to use BSD Labs toll processing?

Yes. You must hold a valid Minnesota cannabis cultivator or manufacturer license issued by the
Office of Cannabis Management (OCM) to use our toll processing service. BSD Labs operates
exclusively B2B with licensed entities.

What types of biomass do you accept?

We accept flower, trim, and shake from licensed Minnesota cannabis cultivators. Toll processing is
an excellent way to maximize the value of your entire harvest — not just premium flower.

What is the minimum volume for toll processing?

Contact us for current minimums. We work with cultivators at various stages of production and can
discuss options based on your specific harvest volume and schedule.

What extraction methods does BSD Labs use?

BSD Labs uses cryo-ethanol and hydrocarbon extraction, paired with multi-pass distillation to
achieve 90%+ THC distillate. The method is selected based on your biomass type and desired
end-product.

How long does toll processing take?

Turnaround time depends on current volume and your biomass characteristics. Contact us to discuss
scheduling — we work with your harvest timeline to minimize any delay between intake and return.

What documentation will I receive?

You receive a full-panel Certificate of Analysis (COA) from an independent lab plus complete batch
documentation including intake records, processing logs, and test results — everything required for
OCM compliance.

How Does it Work?

At the Cannabis Clinic, we’re dedicated to revolutionising modern healthcare through the power of plant-based medicine, including medicinal cannabis.

If you’re exploring natural options to support your health and well-being, CBD oil and THC treatments could be worth considering. Connect with our compassionate and experienced team today to discover personalised care and take the next step in your wellness journey.

1. Book Your Appointment

Select a time and date to book an in-person or telehealth consultation with one of our caring and experienced doctors. We’re proud to offer consultations for patients throughout New Zealand.

2. Speak to a Doctor

Your doctor will review your medical records and discuss the best treatment options with you. You’ll have the opportunity to ask questions, receive guidance, and get a personalised treatment plan tailored to your needs.

3. Medication Delivered

We make accessing your prescription simple. We will securely and confidentially ship your medication to your door or, if you prefer, we can send your script to your local pharmacy.

FAQs

What is medical cannabis?

Medical cannabis refers to therapeutic cannabis-based products that are legally prescribed by a qualified doctor. These products include compounds such as CBD (cannabidiol) and THC (tetrahydrocannabinol), which interact with your body’s natural endocannabinoid system – a system that helps regulate things like sleep, mood, pain, immune function, and inflammation. Unlike recreational cannabis, medical cannabis is used under the guidance of a clinician to support specific health outcomes.

What is CBD oil?

CBD (cannabidiol) oil is one of the most widely used medicinal cannabis products. It’s non-psychoactive, meaning it won’t make you feel “high,” and it has a broad range of potential health benefits. CBD is known for its calming and anti-inflammatory effects, and it’s often used to support sleep, anxiety, pain, and overall well-being. CBD oil is taken orally or under the tongue and is well-tolerated by most people. Learn more: CBD Oil NZ

What are THC and CBD?

THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) and CBD (cannabidiol) are two of the most well-known compounds found in the cannabis plant. THC is the psychoactive ingredient – it may cause a “high,” but also has powerful effects in managing pain, nausea, sleep, and appetite. CBD is non-psychoactive and works with the body’s endocannabinoid system to promote calm, reduce inflammation, and support balance in body and mind. Depending on your condition, one or both compounds may be used in treatment.

Does medicinal cannabis work?

Many patients report significant improvements in symptoms such as chronic pain, insomnia, anxiety, inflammation, and stress when using medicinal cannabis. While it’s not a “cure-all,” clinical studies and patient outcomes continue to show promising results. Medicinal cannabis may be used alone or alongside other treatments, depending on your needs. As with any treatment, effectiveness varies person to person. Booking a consultation with a doctor trained in cannabinoid medicine is the best way to determine if it could work for you.

How does medicinal cannabis work in the body?

Medicinal cannabis works by interacting with the endocannabinoid system (ECS), a natural system in your body that helps regulate pain, mood, sleep, appetite, memory, immune function, and more. The ECS uses chemical messengers (endocannabinoids) to keep your body balanced – this is known as homeostasis. When the ECS is out of balance, you may experience symptoms like pain, anxiety, or poor sleep. Medicinal cannabis contains cannabinoids like CBD and THC, which mimic your body’s natural endocannabinoids to support this balance.Learn more: Understanding Medicinal Cannabis .

Can medicinal cannabis help me?

If you’ve struggled to manage symptoms with conventional treatments or are looking for a plant-based option, medicinal cannabis may be worth exploring. It’s often prescribed for conditions such as chronic pain, anxiety, PTSD, arthritis, sleep issues, and neurological or inflammatory disorders. Our doctors take a case-by-case approach, reviewing your health history and goals before making a recommendation. If you’re curious, book a consultation to see if this is the right path for you: Book Now

What conditions qualify for medical cannabis?

There’s no single “approved list” of qualifying conditions in New Zealand – instead, prescriptions are based on clinical judgement. That said, some of the most common conditions we see at Cannabis Clinic include:

Chronic pain (e.g. arthritis, migraines, injury-related pain)

Anxiety, PTSD and stress-related disorders

Insomnia and other sleep disturbances

Inflammatory conditions like fibromyalgia

Cancer-related symptoms such as nausea, appetite loss, or pain

## FAQs

[ What makes up the cost? ][51]

We understand that price is one of the biggest barriers to accessing medicinal cannabis.
Unfortunately, medicinal cannabis is not currently subsidised by Pharmac, meaning patients must
cover the full cost of treatment themselves.

The products prescribed through our clinic are pharmaceutical-grade, meaning they must meet strict
quality, safety, and manufacturing standards. These standards include third-party testing,
traceability, consistent dosing, and Medsafe approval – all of which contribute to the higher cost
compared to unregulated or overseas products.

The good news? Prices have steadily decreased over the past few years, and we expect this trend to
continue as more products become available. We’re committed to finding the best value options for
your needs and will always work with you to find a cost-effective plan.

Read more: [The Real Cost of Medicinal Cannabis in New Zealand.][52]

[ How much does CBD oil cost? ][53]

CBD oil pricing in New Zealand depends on the concentration, format (oil vs. capsule), and the
dosage recommended by your doctor. While pricing can vary based on individual needs, we strive to
make treatment affordable for everyone. Our doctors and nurses can help you find a product and
dosage that best fit your health needs and budget.

We understand that access to treatment can be challenging, which is why [Lake Road Pharmacy][54]
offers flexible payment options like Afterpay and Zip, allowing you to pay in instalments.

For further assistance in selecting the right treatment plan, we also offer a community support plan
to ensure that you receive the care you need, without financial stress.

[ Book your free call ][55]
[ How much does medicinal cannabis cost in New Zealand? ][56]

The cost of medicinal cannabis treatment varies based on the product prescribed and individual
needs.

Consultation costs:
* Online video consultation: **$79**
* In-person consultation: **$79**

After the initial consultation, ongoing follow-up appointments are generally scheduled **every three
months**. However, depending on your situation, follow-ups may be extended if recommended by your
doctor.

To make access easier, [Lake Road Pharmacy][57] offers flexible payment options like Afterpay and
Zip, so you can pay for your treatment in instalments.

For a personalised cost estimate, we recommend booking a
[free nurse eligibility call][58]. During this call, we’ll discuss your treatment plan and help you
understand the costs involved.

[Learn more about our consultation cost][59].

[ Do you offer payment plans or financial assistance? ][60]

We’re committed to making treatment affordable and accessible:
* To make access easier, [Lake Road Pharmacy][61] offers flexible payment options like Afterpay and
Zip, so you can pay for your treatment in instalments.
* Free nurse eligibility calls to help you understand costs upfront, with no commitment.
* Affordable follow-ups consultation at just $39.
* Flexible prescription lengths, so you can reduce the frequency of repeat visits, tailoring your
treatment plan to your needs.
* Budget-friendly medicine options, carefully selected to fit your lifestyle and health goals.

If cost is a concern, our team is here to work with you and find the most affordable treatment
pathway – whether it’s reviewing lower-dose options or considering a slower introduction plan. In
some cases, our doctors can assist in advocating for employer support or special consideration.

[ Do I need a referral from my doctor to get a prescription? ][62]

No, you do not need a referral. Cannabis Clinic is a direct-to-patient service, meaning anyone in
New Zealand can book a consultation without needing to go through their GP. That said, we encourage
patients to keep their GP informed, as coordinated care leads to better health outcomes.

Our clinic can also communicate with your GP (with your consent) to ensure continuity of care. If
you’re unsure whether medicinal cannabis is appropriate for your condition, we suggest starting with
a free eligibility call with one of our nurses: [Book Now][63].

[ I already have a prescription from my doctor - can you help? ][64]

Yes, we can. If you’ve already received a medicinal cannabis prescription from your GP or another
clinic and would like to continue treatment with us, we’re here to help. You’ll need to book a
consultation with one of our doctors so we can assess your current treatment, review any updates to
your condition, and ensure your medication still suits your needs.

If your existing prescription is still valid, we may be able to continue your treatment plan with
minimal disruption. Patients transferring from another provider are also eligible for a discounted
initial consultation. After you join us, you’ll have access to our full clinical support team, free
nurse check-ins, faster medication fulfillment, and educational resources to help you feel confident
in your care. [Book a consultation now.][65]

[ Why do I need to supply my health summary? ][66]

A [health summary][67] is not required for you to attend your initial consultation, however
supplying your health summary allows our clinical team to fully understand your health history and
ensure any treatment we prescribe is safe, effective, and tailored to your needs. This includes
current and past diagnoses, previous medications, allergies, and any recent test results or
specialist letters.

These notes give your doctor a clear picture of what’s been tried before, what’s worked (or hasn’t),
and whether there are any contraindications with medicinal cannabis. Having this information upfront
helps streamline your consultation, avoids delays, and ensures we meet the legal requirements for
safe prescribing under the Medicinal Cannabis Scheme.

You can request your notes from your GP or download them via your online health portal. If you need
help, our admin team can guide you step-by-step.

[ How long does it take to get a prescription? ][68]

If assessed as being suitable, most patients receive their prescription at the end of their
consultation. In some cases, your doctor may request additional information (such as medical notes
or specialist letters) before finalising the script. Once your prescription is issued, it’s sent to
the pharmacy and can usually be processed and shipped within 1–2 business days.

# Our Doctors & Nurses

### Pioneering Medicinal Cannabis Care in New Zealand

## Welcome to the **Cannabis Clinic.**

##### We are proud to be revolutionising healthcare in New Zealand through the power of medicinal
##### cannabis. By challenging traditional norms and embracing plant-based medicine, our
##### forward-thinking doctors and remarkable patients are shaping a future where natural treatments
##### are accessible and transformative.

Our mission is to empower every New Zealander to achieve better health and wellness, naturally. For
many of our patients, this is their first step into exploring medicinal cannabis, and we’re here to
guide them every step of the way – from consultations and personalised treatment plans to ongoing
care and shared success stories.

Since our founding in 2018, we’ve helped over 50,000 Kiwis, from children to those receiving
palliative care. Our dedicated team of compassionate doctors, nurses, and administrative staff
ensures each patient receives exceptional, affordable care tailored to their unique needs.

All our clinicians are registered with the [Medical Council of New Zealand][36] or the Nursing
Council of New Zealand and belong to esteemed Royal Colleges, including [Physicians][37], [General
Practice][38], Public Health Medicine, [Neurology][39], Psychiatry, [Anaesthesia][40], [Urgent
Care][41] and more. Their expertise reflects our commitment to the highest standards of care.

As New Zealand’s largest medicinal cannabis clinic, we are leading the way in redefining modern
healthcare. Together, let’s embark on a journey toward better health, greater wellness, and a
brighter future for all.

## Helpdesk Q&A
* [Information About Medicinal Cannabis][38]
* [Legality and Regulations][39]
* [Consultations and Prescriptions][40]
* [Usage, Side Effects and Safety][41]
* [From the Community][42]

[ What is medical cannabis? ][43]

Medical cannabis refers to therapeutic cannabis-based products that are legally prescribed by a
qualified doctor. These products include compounds such as CBD (cannabidiol) and THC
(tetrahydrocannabinol), which interact with your body’s natural endocannabinoid system – a system
that helps regulate things like sleep, mood, pain, immune function, and inflammation. Unlike
recreational cannabis, medical cannabis is used under the guidance of a clinician to support
specific health outcomes.

[ What is CBD oil? ][44]

CBD (cannabidiol) oil is one of the most widely used medicinal cannabis products. It’s
non-psychoactive, meaning it won’t make you feel “high,” and it has a broad range of potential
health benefits. CBD is known for its calming and anti-inflammatory effects, and it’s often used to
support sleep, anxiety, pain, and overall well-being. CBD oil is taken orally or under the tongue
and is well-tolerated by most people. Learn more:[ CBD Oil NZ][45]

[ What are THC and CBD? ][46]

THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) and CBD (cannabidiol) are two of the most well-known compounds found in
the cannabis plant. THC is the psychoactive ingredient – it may cause a “high,” but also has
powerful effects in managing pain, nausea, sleep, and appetite. CBD is non-psychoactive and works
with the body’s endocannabinoid system to promote calm, reduce inflammation, and support balance in
body and mind. Depending on your condition, one or both compounds may be used in treatment.

[ Does medicinal cannabis work? ][47]

Many patients report significant improvements in symptoms such as chronic pain, insomnia, anxiety,
inflammation, and stress when using medicinal cannabis. While it’s not a “cure-all,” clinical
studies and patient outcomes continue to show promising results. Medicinal cannabis may be used
alone or alongside other treatments, depending on your needs. As with any treatment, effectiveness
varies person to person. Booking a consultation with a doctor trained in cannabinoid medicine is the
best way to determine if it could work for you.

[ How does medicinal cannabis work in the body? ][48]

Medicinal cannabis works by interacting with the endocannabinoid system (ECS), a natural system in
your body that helps regulate pain, mood, sleep, appetite, memory, immune function, and more. The
ECS uses chemical messengers (endocannabinoids) to keep your body balanced – this is known as
homeostasis. When the ECS is out of balance, you may experience symptoms like pain, anxiety, or poor
sleep. Medicinal cannabis contains cannabinoids like CBD and THC, which mimic your body’s natural
endocannabinoids to support this balance.Learn more: [Understanding Medicinal Cannabis][49].

[ Can medicinal cannabis help me? ][50]

If you’ve struggled to manage symptoms with conventional treatments or are looking for a plant-based
option, medicinal cannabis may be worth exploring. It’s often prescribed for conditions such as
chronic pain, anxiety, PTSD, arthritis, sleep issues, and neurological or inflammatory disorders.
Our doctors take a case-by-case approach, reviewing your health history and goals before making a
recommendation. If you’re curious, book a consultation to see if this is the right path for you:
[Book Now][51]

[ What conditions qualify for medical cannabis? ][52]

There’s no single “approved list” of qualifying conditions in New Zealand – instead, prescriptions
are based on clinical judgement. That said, some of the most common conditions we see at Cannabis
Clinic include:
* Chronic pain (e.g. arthritis, migraines, injury-related pain)
* Anxiety, PTSD and stress-related disorders
* Insomnia and other sleep disturbances
* Inflammatory conditions like fibromyalgia
* Cancer-related symptoms such as nausea, appetite loss, or pain
* Neurological conditions such as epilepsy, MS, or Parkinson’s

If you’re unsure whether your condition qualifies, our nurse team can guide you through the process
and help you book with a doctor.

[ What medicinal cannabis products are available in NZ? ][53]

Medicinal cannabis in New Zealand includes CBD oils, capsules, and dried flower for vaporisation.
Some products contain THC or a combination of THC and CBD, depending on your needs and what your
doctor prescribes. Each product must meet strict quality standards set by Medsafe, and availability
may vary over time. We’ll work with you to find the best option for your condition, symptoms, and
lifestyle.

[ What types of medical cannabis do you prescribe? ][54]

Our clinic prescribes a variety of formats to suit different needs:
* CBD-only oil (most commonly prescribed)
* CBD/THC oil in varying ratios
* THC-only oil in certain clinical cases
* CBD or THC capsules
* Dried flower (for a tea or vaporisation only – not for smoking)

The format and cannabinoid content are carefully chosen based on your medical history, treatment
goals, and preferences.

[ What does medical cannabis taste like? ][55]

The taste of medical cannabis products can vary. Oils often have an earthy, herbal, or slightly
bitter flavour due to the plant compounds. Some people find this taste strong, while others don’t
mind it. If the taste is an issue, capsules offer a flavourless alternative, and vaporised flower
has a more aromatic, herbal profile that some patients find more pleasant.

[ Does medical cannabis make you ‘high’? ][56]

It depends on the type and dose. CBD does not cause any intoxicating effects and is safe for daytime
use. THC, on the other hand, may cause a “high” at higher doses. Our doctors carefully tailor THC
prescriptions to minimise unwanted effects and support symptom relief. In most cases, patients using
prescribed THC report feelings of relaxation, improved sleep, or pain relief – not a recreational
high.

[ Does medical cannabis smell? ][57]

CBD oils and capsules generally have no noticeable smell. However, dried cannabis flower may have a
distinct herbal or earthy scent, especially when vaporised. This smell is usually mild and doesn’t
linger for long. If you’re concerned about odour, our team can suggest low-scent or alternative
formats.

[ Is medical cannabis legal in NZ? ][58]

All Medicinal Cannabis products (both CBD and THC) are classed as unapproved, section 29 medications
in New Zealand. This means they can be legally prescribed by a registered doctor for a patient,
however they have not been formally approved or recommended for any condition (except multiple
sclerosis and specific seizure disorders). As evidence for their use in different conditions
evolves, we hope to see them approved for more conditions and their use more widespread. Learn more:
[Is CBD Oil Legal in NZ][59]

[ Can I take my medical cannabis in public? ][60]

Yes, if it’s prescribed to you, you are legally allowed to carry it with you in public. However,
your medicine must be in its original packaging and clearly labelled with your name and dosage
instructions. Using your medicine (especially any containing THC) in public is not recommended, as
this could draw unwanted attention or cause confusion. As a general rule, treat your medication with
the same discretion as you would any prescription medicine.

[ Can I drive while using medicinal cannabis in NZ? ][61]

If you are using CBD-only products, you can legally drive as long as you are not impaired. CBD is
non-intoxicating and does not affect motor function or cognition. However, if your prescription
includes THC, we usually recommend waiting at least 8–10 hours before driving to ensure it has
cleared your system and you are not impaired. If you feel drowsy, slow to react, or otherwise
affected, do not drive. Roadside drug testing is conducted in New Zealand and can detect THC.
Driving while impaired can result in legal consequences. Learn more: [Changes to Random Roadside
Saliva Drug Testing in NZ: What it Means for Medicinal Cannabis Patients][62]

[ Will medicinal cannabis show up on a drug test? ][63]

Yes, if your medication contains THC, it may result in a positive drug test. CBD-only products will
not typically show up on drug tests, but some tests may not distinguish between cannabinoids. If you
are in a safety-sensitive role or subject to workplace drug testing, we recommend speaking with your
employer in advance. Cannabis Clinic can provide supporting letters and documentation for patients,
but we cannot override employer policies.

[ Can I take medicinal cannabis if I am pregnant or breastfeeding? ][64]

No, we do not recommend the use of medicinal cannabis during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. There
is currently insufficient scientific evidence to confirm the safety of cannabinoids during these
times, and international health guidelines recommend avoiding all cannabis products during pregnancy
and lactation.

We also recommend ceasing cannabis products around 3 months before trying for pregnancy – this is
valid for both individuals with sperm and those with eggs. If you have questions about treatment
options while pregnant, speak to your doctor or midwife.

[ Can I travel with my medication? ][65]

Yes, but the rules differ for domestic and international travel. If you’re travelling within New
Zealand, you can legally carry your prescribed medicinal cannabis as long as it remains in its
original pharmacy packaging with a clear label showing your name, dosing instructions, and
prescribing doctor. We recommend taking a copy of your prescription or treatment summary with you,
especially when travelling through airports. We can also provide a letter of support for travel, for
extra peace of mind.

If you’re flying, pack your medication in your carry-on bag and ensure it remains easily accessible
if requested by security. If you have questions about domestic travel, our nursing team can help
guide you before your trip.

International travel is much more complex. Medicinal cannabis remains illegal in many countries, and
even CBD-only products may be restricted or banned. Some countries have strict penalties for
possession, regardless of whether your medicine is legally prescribed in New Zealand. For this
reason, we strongly advise not travelling internationally with medicinal cannabis unless you have
checked the regulations in your destination country and layovers and obtained the appropriate travel
permits, where possible.

Learn more about travelling with medicinal cannabis in our blog: [Travelling with medicinal cannabis
blog post here][66]

[ Do I need to tell my GP about my prescription? ][67]

No, it’s not legally required to inform your GP about your medicinal cannabis prescription. However,
at Cannabis Clinic, we strongly recommend open communication between your prescriber and primary
care provider. Coordinated care

[ What is medical cannabis? ][43]

Medical cannabis refers to therapeutic cannabis-based products that are legally prescribed by a
qualified doctor. These products include compounds such as CBD (cannabidiol) and THC
(tetrahydrocannabinol), which interact with your body’s natural endocannabinoid system – a system
that helps regulate things like sleep, mood, pain, immune function, and inflammation. Unlike
recreational cannabis, medical cannabis is used under the guidance of a clinician to support
specific health outcomes.

[ What is CBD oil? ][44]

CBD (cannabidiol) oil is one of the most widely used medicinal cannabis products. It’s
non-psychoactive, meaning it won’t make you feel “high,” and it has a broad range of potential
health benefits. CBD is known for its calming and anti-inflammatory effects, and it’s often used to
support sleep, anxiety, pain, and overall well-being. CBD oil is taken orally or under the tongue
and is well-tolerated by most people. Learn more:[ CBD Oil NZ][45]

[ What are THC and CBD? ][46]

THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) and CBD (cannabidiol) are two of the most well-known compounds found in
the cannabis plant. THC is the psychoactive ingredient – it may cause a “high,” but also has
powerful effects in managing pain, nausea, sleep, and appetite. CBD is non-psychoactive and works
with the body’s endocannabinoid system to promote calm, reduce inflammation, and support balance in
body and mind. Depending on your condition, one or both compounds may be used in treatment.

[ Does medicinal cannabis work? ][47]

Many patients report significant improvements in symptoms such as chronic pain, insomnia, anxiety,
inflammation, and stress when using medicinal cannabis. While it’s not a “cure-all,” clinical
studies and patient outcomes continue to show promising results. Medicinal cannabis may be used
alone or alongside other treatments, depending on your needs. As with any treatment, effectiveness
varies person to person. Booking a consultation with a doctor trained in cannabinoid medicine is the
best way to determine if it could work for you.

[ How does medicinal cannabis work in the body? ][48]

Medicinal cannabis works by interacting with the endocannabinoid system (ECS), a natural system in
your body that helps regulate pain, mood, sleep, appetite, memory, immune function, and more. The
ECS uses chemical messengers (endocannabinoids) to keep your body balanced – this is known as
homeostasis. When the ECS is out of balance, you may experience symptoms like pain, anxiety, or poor
sleep. Medicinal cannabis contains cannabinoids like CBD and THC, which mimic your body’s natural
endocannabinoids to support this balance.Learn more: [Understanding Medicinal Cannabis][49].

[ Can medicinal cannabis help me? ][50]

If you’ve struggled to manage symptoms with conventional treatments or are looking for a plant-based
option, medicinal cannabis may be worth exploring. It’s often prescribed for conditions such as
chronic pain, anxiety, PTSD, arthritis, sleep issues, and neurological or inflammatory disorders.
Our doctors take a case-by-case approach, reviewing your health history and goals before making a
recommendation. If you’re curious, book a consultation to see if this is the right path for you:
[Book Now][51]

[ What conditions qualify for medical cannabis? ][52]

There’s no single “approved list” of qualifying conditions in New Zealand – instead, prescriptions
are based on clinical judgement. That said, some of the most common conditions we see at Cannabis
Clinic include:
* Chronic pain (e.g. arthritis, migraines, injury-related pain)
* Anxiety, PTSD and stress-related disorders
* Insomnia and other sleep disturbances
* Inflammatory conditions like fibromyalgia
* Cancer-related symptoms such as nausea, appetite loss, or pain
* Neurological conditions such as epilepsy, MS, or Parkinson’s

If you’re unsure whether your condition qualifies, our nurse team can guide you through the process
and help you book with a doctor.

[ What medicinal cannabis products are available in NZ? ][53]

Medicinal cannabis in New Zealand includes CBD oils, capsules, and dried flower for vaporisation.
Some products contain THC or a combination of THC and CBD, depending on your needs and what your
doctor prescribes. Each product must meet strict quality standards set by Medsafe, and availability
may vary over time. We’ll work with you to find the best option for your condition, symptoms, and
lifestyle.

[ What types of medical cannabis do you prescribe? ][54]

Our clinic prescribes a variety of formats to suit different needs:
* CBD-only oil (most commonly prescribed)
* CBD/THC oil in varying ratios
* THC-only oil in certain clinical cases
* CBD or THC capsules
* Dried flower (for a tea or vaporisation only – not for smoking)

The format and cannabinoid content are carefully chosen based on your medical history, treatment
goals, and preferences.

[ What does medical cannabis taste like? ][55]

The taste of medical cannabis products can vary. Oils often have an earthy, herbal, or slightly
bitter flavour due to the plant compounds. Some people find this taste strong, while others don’t
mind it. If the taste is an issue, capsules offer a flavourless alternative, and vaporised flower
has a more aromatic, herbal profile that some patients find more pleasant.

[ Does medical cannabis make you ‘high’? ][56]

It depends on the type and dose. CBD does not cause any intoxicating effects and is safe for daytime
use. THC, on the other hand, may cause a “high” at higher doses. Our doctors carefully tailor THC
prescriptions to minimise unwanted effects and support symptom relief. In most cases, patients using
prescribed THC report feelings of relaxation, improved sleep, or pain relief – not a recreational
high.

[ Does medical cannabis smell? ][57]

CBD oils and capsules generally have no noticeable smell. However, dried cannabis flower may have a
distinct herbal or earthy scent, especially when vaporised. This smell is usually mild and doesn’t
linger for long. If you’re concerned about odour, our team can suggest low-scent or alternative
formats.

## CORPORATE OVERVIEW.

Cannabis Science, Inc. takes advantage of its unique understanding of metabolic processes to provide
innovative treatment options for unmet medical needs.

Cannabis use has an extensive history dating back thousands of years, and currently, there are
thousands of peer-reviewed scientific publications that document the underlying biochemical pathways
that cannabinoids modulate.

At Cannabis Science, we use an inquiring approach to discover and develop novel cannabinoid-based
therapies to improve patients’ lives. From the initiation, our founders have been committed to
fostering and maintaining a bold, pioneering spirit fostering the true nature of innovation from
which cutting-edge ideas flourish and translate into evidence-based solutions.

We are dedicated to working closely with local, national and international regulatory agencies to
provide access to high quality, first-class cannabinoid pharmaceuticals to those critically in need
of new treatments for life-threatening and debilitating conditions. Cannabis Science’s clinical
trial material comes from the cultivation and production facilities that are cGMP compliant,
surpassing high quality standard industrial and food processing requirements.

The Company works with leading experts in drug development, medicinal characterization, and clinical
research to develop, produce, and commercialize novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of
multiple critical ailments from cancer and infections to age-related illnesses and neurobehavioral
disorders.

Our products, broadly described, are medical cannabinoid formulations developed from one or more of
the cannabinoid compounds found in the cannabis plant. Our immediate focus is to treat one of the
most important diseases in the world, cancer.

In 2013, Cannabis Science submitted patent application N2010968 in Europe entitled "Composition for
the Treatment of Neurobehavioral Disorders" (CS-NEURO-1). The subject of the patent is the
development of cannabinoid-based formulations to treat a variety of neurobehavioral disorders.

### BASIS & PHILOSOPHY.

Cannabis plants have an extensive history of medical and agricultural use dating back thousands of
years. To date, hundreds of natural constituents covering several chemical classes have been
isolated and identified from the Cannabis plant.

***SOME KEY PHYTOCANNABINOIDS:***
* tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)
* cannabidiol (CBD)
* cannabigerol (CBG)
* cannabichromene (CBC)
* cannabinol (CBN)

These cannabinoids belong to the chemical class of terpenophenolics, of which 85 have been uniquely
identified in cannabis, including the most psychoactive cannabinoid, THC. Some applications of
cannabinoids have been well established in peer-reviewed literature such as for alleviating nausea
and stimulating the appetite for people with AIDS and cancer. Other well-known uses include easing
chronic pain and reducing muscle spasms associated with multiple sclerosis and spinal cord injuries.

The pharmacology of THC has been widely studied, while many other identified cannabinoids are still
poorly characterized pharmacologically and biologically, with new activities for cannabinoids
consistently being discovered.

Cannabis Science is developing novel cannabis-based approaches to treat the world’s most deadly
illnesses. We learn from patients about the healing properties of cannabis medicines. Our immediate
focus is the development of cutting-edge cancer treatments.

The Company’s future endeavors include infectious illnesses, neurobehavioral disorders including
attention deficit disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder; and an application of the
anti-inflammatory activities of cannabis in the management of age-related illnesses.

The endocannabinoid system possessed by all vertebrates regulates all body systems and maintains
homeostasis. As such, the mechanisms of phytocannabinoids’ biological impact are multidimensional.

While concentrating on our core activities of discovering and developing treatments that will make a
meaningful difference in patients’ lives, we remain mindful that we have other responsibilities to
the clinicians who utilize our drugs, health authorities around the world, our shareholders, our
employees, and the communities in which we live and work. We continually strive to improve our
corporate responsibility standards and activities, implementing comprehensive ethical standards and
undertaking patient and community progressive initiatives.

These principles reflect the mission of Cannabis Science to provide innovative therapeutics for
unmet medical needs.

As the industry leader, Cannabis Science consults and leads other emerging businesses that Cannabis
Science believes has a preferred business model, one which will mature into a key business model in
the future. Our consulting is on the entire "seed to sale" process with a focus on biopharmaceutical
development.

Cannabis Science is one of the longest standing companies in the cannabis business.

We feel that the correct way is to look at the industry from a bio-pharmaceutical standpoint, in a
manner that allows cannabinoid-based products to modulate the endocannabinoid system to treat
multiple conditions. Scientifically, we know this is the beginning of one of the greatest expansions
of medicine and industry we will ever experience in our lifetime.

the Treatment of Neurobehavioral Disorders" (CS-NEURO-1). The subject of the patent is the
development of cannabinoid-based formulations to treat a variety of neurobehavioral disorders.

### BASIS & PHILOSOPHY.

Cannabis plants have an extensive history of medical and agricultural use dating back thousands of
years. To date, hundreds of natural constituents covering several chemical classes have been
isolated and identified from the Cannabis plant.

***SOME KEY PHYTOCANNABINOIDS:***
* tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)
* cannabidiol (CBD)
* cannabigerol (CBG)
* cannabichromene (CBC)
* cannabinol (CBN)

These cannabinoids belong to the chemical class of terpenophenolics, of which 85 have been uniquely
identified in cannabis, including the most psychoactive cannabinoid, THC. Some applications of
cannabinoids have been well established in peer-reviewed literature such as for alleviating nausea
and stimulating the appetite for people with AIDS and cancer. Other well-known uses include easing
chronic pain and reducing muscle spasms associated with multiple sclerosis and spinal cord injuries.

The pharmacology of THC has been widely studied, while many other identified cannabinoids are still
poorly characterized pharmacologically and biologically, with new activities for cannabinoids
consistently being discovered.

Cannabis Science is developing novel cannabis-based approaches to treat the world’s most deadly
illnesses. We learn from patients about the healing properties of cannabis medicines. Our immediate
focus is the development of cutting-edge cancer treatments.

The Company’s future endeavors include infectious illnesses, neurobehavioral disorders including
attention deficit disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder; and an application of the
anti-inflammatory activities of cannabis in the management of age-related illnesses.

The endocannabinoid system possessed by all vertebrates regulates all body systems and maintains
homeostasis. As such, the mechanisms of phytocannabinoids’ biological impact are multidimensional.

While concentrating on our core activities of discovering and developing treatments that will make a
meaningful difference in patients’ lives, we remain mindful that we have other responsibilities to
the clinicians who utilize our drugs, health authorities around the world, our shareholders, our
employees, and the communities in which we live and work. We continually strive to improve our
corporate responsibility standards and activities, implementing comprehensive ethical standards and
undertaking patient and community progressive initiatives.

These principles reflect the mission of Cannabis Science to provide innovative therapeutics for
unmet medical needs.

As the industry leader, Cannabis Science consults and leads other emerging businesses that Cannabis
Science believes has a preferred business model, one which will mature into a key business model in
the future. Our consulting is on the entire "seed to sale" process with a focus on biopharmaceutical
development.

Cannabis Science is one of the longest standing companies in the cannabis business.

We feel that the correct way is to look at the industry from a bio-pharmaceutical standpoint, in a
manner that allows cannabinoid-based products to modulate the endocannabinoid system to treat
multiple conditions. Scientifically, we know this is the beginning of one of the greatest expansions
of medicine and industry we will ever experience in our lifetime.
